newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby union-Campo feted after 100th test.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Campo feted after 100th test.

text.p: David Campese, Australia's most capped rugby union player, was feted by dignitaries on Thursday after playing his 100th test and will soon add tea with England's Queen Elizabeth to his list of honours.

"Australians and all rugby supporters throughout the world have marvelled (at) and admired your feats with a football ever since your first international for Australia in 1982," Australian Prime Minister John Howard said in a message of congratulations sent to Campese after Wednesday's test.
"With a world record of 64 tries and a total of 315 points scored throughout your illustrious test career, you are undoubtedly one of the greatest players of all time," he said.
Australia's Governor-General Sir William Deane -- Queen Elizabeth's representative in the former British colony -- praised Campese for the pleasure he gave fans.
"Over the years...you have been a mainstay of the rugby union, an ornament of Australian sport and a credit to Australia," Deane wrote in a letter to Campese.
Campese was unable to add to his tally of tries during Australia's 40-18 defeat of Italy in Padua. Only Frenchman Philippe Sella, with 111 caps, has played more test matches.
Campese's family traces its origins to northern Italy and the great winger had about 20 relatives watching the match.

The Wallabies had hoped to meet the Pope on Thursday but were disappointed to learn this week that the meeting had been cancelled because the Pontiff was recovering from surgery to remove his appendix.

But Australia's team management confirmed that Campese and his teammates were booked to have afternoon tea with Queen Elizabeth at Buckingham Palace on December 3, two days after the final test of their tour against Wales at Cardiff Arms Park.
